pairs.difference: A: the brass lamp is a rich warm gold-orange with a pale blue-white chimney, set against a yellow-green burst. B: the iron key is an almost grey brown-grey with almost no color (subject chroma 0.023, far below the real 0.08 minimum), and the whole card is about one hue family (green, 1.15). The key's shadows are just darker grey.
pairs.fix: Paint the key as warm aged bronze or rusty iron with visible copper-orange and brown tones on the bow and shaft. Let a cool blue-violet reflection show in the shadow side.

pairs.difference: A: a warm brown wooden clock with a cream face and a gold pendulum on a green studio backdrop. The hero is warm and the background cool. B: a blue vending machine on a magenta-purple backdrop, so a cool hero sits on a cool neighbouring hue. The warm share is almost zero (0.026, below the real 0.13 minimum). The only warm notes are the small cans.
pairs.fix: Put the blue vending machine on a warm yellow-orange backdrop, or make the machine body a warm red. Fill the shelves with warm-colored cans.

pairs.difference: A: a dark purple-black hat with one orange band and a gold buckle on a purple field. The palette is restrained and most of it rests on muted dark tones. B: the sneakers are pushed to pure hues everywhere: cobalt uppers, neon lime collars, teal laces, magenta and orange sole stripes, on an orange-and-yellow set. That makes 5.5 hue families, above the real maximum of 4.8, and no area is muted for the eye to rest on.
pairs.fix: Draw the sneakers in two main colors, blue uppers and white soles, with one small accent color. Drop the neon lime, magenta and teal trims, and make the soles a plain cool white.

pairs.difference: A: a warm honey-wood rocking chair with a green cushion against a cool blue striped wall, the typical warm-hero-on-cool-backdrop pattern. B: the cat is near-black with almost no color (subject chroma 0.036). It sits on a purple-pink gradient, and the stone ledge is also tinted purple. The shadows turn flat black-violet (shadow chroma kept 0.42, below the real 0.49 minimum), so the whole card reads as one purple wash.
pairs.fix: Give the black cat cool blue-violet highlights and warm brown fur tones. Make the stone ledge a neutral warm grey instead of purple, and let the shadows keep some deep blue color instead of going flat black.

pairs.difference: A: a red velvet box with a cream lining and a gold coin against a cool cyan burst, with one small blue ribbon accent. B: the purple mask sits on an all-yellow sunburst, and the gold trim, the yellow background and the orange-pink feather all pull warm (warm share 0.99, far above the real 0.73 maximum). The only cool note is the mask's purple.
pairs.fix: Keep the purple mask but put it on a cool blue or teal sunburst. Make the feather pink-magenta rather than orange.

pairs.difference: A: green binoculars with deep blue lenses on warm honey floorboards. The hero and backdrop are opposite in temperature. B: yellow straw and a brown handle lie on yellow-green grass. The hero hue sits right next to the backdrop hue, and the card collapses to about 1.5 hue families (the real minimum is 3.0). The only separate accent is the small red binding.
pairs.fix: Set the broom on a cool blue or blue-grey stone floor instead of yellow-green grass, or make the grass a deeper, cooler blue-green so the straw-yellow broom stands apart.

pairs.difference: A: a clear jar of candies in pink, orange and purple wrappers on a muted grey-brown wooden table against a sky-blue backdrop. The table gives the eye a neutral rest. B: the caravan body is a warm yellowish cream rather than a cool white, with orange stripes. It sits on a very loud magenta-violet backdrop (background chroma 0.199, above the real 0.178 maximum) and yellow-green grass, so the background is louder than the hero.
pairs.fix: Paint the caravan body clean cool white with light blue-grey shadows. Turn the purple backdrop down to a softer, less saturated lilac or sky blue.

pairs.difference: A: a green topiary sits in front of a green hedge, on green lawn, under a blue sky. The hero repeats the backdrop hue, and the warm share is almost zero (0.046, below the real minimum). Even the stone ring and path are bleached to pale grey. B: a blue snorkel and mask on warm orange planks next to teal water, a clear cool-hero / warm-ground split with a single purple accent on the mouthpiece.
pairs.fix: Put the green topiary in front of a warm terracotta wall or warm sandstone paving. Make the planter ring warm beige, and keep the hedge out of the background.

pairs.difference: A: a motel scene at night. A pink neon sign, a yellow arrow and a green sign sit against a deep navy sky, with warm-lit windows. Several hue families each play a distinct role. B: a black lamp post with almost no color (subject chroma 0.066) stands on purple-tinted cobbles under a violet sky. Every shadow goes to the same dull violet (shadow chroma kept 0.44, below the real 0.61 minimum), and the only warm note is the lamp glow.
pairs.fix: Paint the lamp post dark green or deep blue metal with a brass trim. Make the cobblestones warm grey-tan, and keep the sky violet only near the horizon.

pairs.difference: A: the fountain stone is a warm cream-beige, the same yellowish neutral the lessons' generated computers use. It stands on a yellow striped wall and peach paving, so the hero and backdrop share a warm hue (warm share 0.86, above the real 0.85 maximum). The cyan water is the only cool note. B: an orange pumpkin with a green stem on weathered grey-brown wood against a cool blue striped wall, the classic warm-on-cool layout.
pairs.fix: Draw the fountain in cool light-grey stone with blue-grey shadows. Put it on a cool blue or teal striped backdrop instead of yellow.

pairs.difference: A: a cool lavender-grey stone wall around a warm brown wooden window with a single candle glow, against a navy night sky. The stone is a large neutral resting area. B: red brick pillars, a copper-red gate, pink-peach paving and cream caps all sit in one red-orange family. The green and blue around them are background only, and the hero has no cool counter-note inside it. The evidence is weak.
pairs.fix: Make the gate dark green or black wrought iron. Turn the paving a neutral grey stone so that the brick red is the only warm area.

pairs.difference: A: a cobalt-blue snorkel with a purple mouthpiece on orange planks beside teal water: a cool hero on warm ground with one accent. B: the marble lion is almost colorless (subject chroma 0.027, far below the real 0.05 minimum) and leans to a warm cream rather than cool white. Its shadows are flat beige-grey, and the bright green lawn and trees out-color the hero.
pairs.fix: Paint the lion in cool white marble with pale blue-grey shadows and faint grey veins. Put it on warm sandy stone paving with less saturated green around it, so the statue stays the brightest, cleanest shape.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away on palette in three ways. First, white and grey materials (plastic, stone, marble, caravan shells) drift to a warm cream or beige, where real cards keep them cool white or lavender-grey. Second, the hero repeats the backdrop's hue or temperature: a green topiary in green hedges, a purple cat on purple, a beige fountain on yellow, a blue machine on magenta. Real cards set a warm hero against a cool ground. Third, whole cards collapse to one tint, either an almost colorless hero (key, lion, lamp post, cat) whose shadows go dull, or the opposite, pure-hue overload with neon accents on everything (sneakers).
